parsed.basis: Malta's national regime applies uniformly in Żurrieq: same-sex conduct was decriminalised in 1973, gender identity is constitutionally protected, and discrimination and hate-crime provisions cover gender identity and expression. Legal gender recognition requires no surgery, nonbinary identity is recognised, bathroom access is legally protected, and conversion therapy is banned. Żurrieq is a small, inland, residential town with a traditional Catholic festa culture, limited tourist infrastructure and few visible LGBTQ venues or support services, so a visitor may encounter more curiosity, staring and conservative disapproval than in Valletta or Sliema. No local law or enforcement practice distinguishes it, and police, courts, health care and border procedures operate nationally, though underreporting of harassment affects Malta generally.
